messages.author: d718c6bb1db28db2
messages.subject: Re: Minimun number of sightings for a robust analysis
parts:
It is a rough guideline. Accurate estimates of distances don't really
reduce the number needed, although if you can ensure that virtually all
animals are detected for some distance from the line, so that the
detection function has a wide 'shoulder', you can get away with fewer
detections and still have reliable estimation. The software will work
on smaller sample sizes. Whether you get a good estimate of density or
abundance with small samples depends on a range of factors, one of them
being luck. e.g. if your detection function has a wide shoulder, but
your sample size is small, the histogram of detection distances may be
quite spiked (no shoulder) purely through chance, and then estimation
can be very unreliable.

Steve Buckland
